playlist.name: hermes{YYYYMMDD}
playlist.description: Discovery playlist auto-curated from your listening profile

a-dnb.name: Neurofunk, techstep, and experimental DnB
a-dnb.baseline: Dark/technical DnB, neurofunk, techstep, experimental DnB, and exceptional halftime — the Noisia, Vision, Blackout, and Critical lineage.
a-dnb.research: This lane releases less often: 1–3 excellent, current fits beat padding with generic DnB, liquid DnB, or weakly related material.

b-ukg.name: UK garage, bassline, and speed garage
b-ukg.baseline: UK garage, bassline, speed garage, 2-step, organ-bass garage, and credible garage-house hybrids. Prioritize the Sammy Virji/Katy B side of the profile.
b-ukg.research: Night Bass, Insomniac and Toolroom count only where the specific release has real garage/bassline character, not just a house track with a garage vocal chop.
b-ukg.exclude: Straightforward tech house, generic slap house, and pop-house that only uses a surface garage vocal sample. The release needs real garage/bassline/2-step rhythm and bass programming.

c-bass.name: Bass house, tech house, and electro-club
c-bass.baseline: Bass house, muscular tech house, electro-house revival, dirty club tracks, and high-energy groove-forward house. Reference points for the sound: James Hype, Disco Lines, tougher John Summit material, and Diplo-style dance-floor production — they describe the sound, not artists to avoid.
c-bass.exclude: Melodic/progressive house, generic pop EDM, and UK garage/bassline (another lane). The release needs real bass-house/tech-house/electro-club energy, not just a house tag.

d-exp.name: Experimental bass, 140, and future-facing club
d-exp.baseline: Experimental bass, glitchy/sample-based production, experimental trap, future bass, 140/deep dubstep, left-field dubstep, breaks, and bass-driven club hybrids. Reference points: adventurous Skrillex, ISOxo, Flume, Noisia-style sound design, nimino, and genuinely distinctive Fred again..-adjacent sample craft.
d-exp.exclude: Formulaic melodic future bass, generic brostep, and low-effort piano-vocal "Fred again.. adjacent" matches. The release needs real experimental, glitchy or left-field character.

e-indie.name: Indie electronic and crossover grooves
e-indie.baseline: Indie electronic, chillwave, indie dance, synth-pop, alternative R&B, electro-soul, sample-led electronic pop, and electronic/alternative crossover with strong songwriting or groove. Reference points: Toro y Moi, Balu Brigada, Maverick Sabre, Artemas, Whethan, GRiZ's soulful side, and selected Oliver Tree-type crossover.
e-indie.exclude: Generic bedroom pop, straight singer-songwriter tracks with little electronic identity, and rock without meaningful electronic overlap.

f-melodic.name: Selective melodic, orchestral, and progressive electronic
f-melodic.baseline: Worakls-adjacent melodic/progressive electronic, orchestral or cinematic electronic, and only unusually distinctive melodic house/techno — a narrow, selective lane, not a general melodic-techno catch-all. Reference points: Worakls, Hungry Music, relevant Anjunadeep, This Never Happened, Stil vor Talent, and Cercle-adjacent material with real compositional depth.
f-melodic.research: Include a candidate only when its text sources support a distinctive compositional, orchestral, progressive, or unusual-production angle; a bare "melodic techno" tag isn't enough.
f-melodic.exclude: Tale Of Us, Anyma, other major Afterlife flagship artists, and generic high-volume Afterlife-style material.
